title: Our Father, Who in Heaven Art
description: Our Father, Who in Heaven Art in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Thomas Whittemore wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 438 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Same”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Our Fa-ther, who in hea-ven art, All hal-lowed be thy name: Thy king-dom come, thy will be done, On earth, in heaven the same.

lines: Our Father, who in heaven art,
Thy kingdom come, thy will be done,
On earth, in heaven the same.
Give us this day our daily bread,
Thine is the kingdom, glory, power

licence: Public domain: Thomas Whittemore died in 1861.
credits: Words by Thomas Whittemore (1800–1861), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
